correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=2, the real edge projection BL^+B^T is defined unambiguously. The tridiagonal Green formula G_ij=U_min V_max/(sinh(gamma)sinh(n gamma)), cosh(gamma)=2, is proved by its recurrence and boundary equations. A unit-rung current yields the exact absolute row sum R_k=1+2(2G_kk-G_1k-G_nk). A unit-rail current decomposes into a single symmetric cut step and an antisymmetric dipole, yielding T_k=2-d_1+d_n<2 with d=G(e_k-e_{k+1}); all signs and cut telescoping are justified. A strict hyperbolic derivative locates central maximizing rungs, with n=2,3,4 handled exactly and n>=5 settled via the strict two bound. The recurrence and n-to-infinity parity defect follow from exact hyperbolic identities. On-path exact checker tested 4,448 identities and agrees with all formulas, but finite tests are not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The canonical edge gradient projection is a natural stability operator in finite-dimensional real graph Hodge theory and electrical routing. Exact induced maximum norms distinguish bounded input edge-signal amplification from spectral projector norm 1. The theorem provides all-size exact rational constants, classifies all maximizing edge orbits, proves a strict sub-2 rail bound and the exact n=5 first super-2 cutoff, and computes the sharp constant 1+2/sqrt(3) with distinct finite-size parity corrections. Those new comparisons are not just a table of diagonal effective resistances or a routine matrix normalization.
